name: GMOOCA Gaming Manager 2
summary: Windows software that connects to your machines over SAS or G2S and keeps track of meters, events, tickets and credits. Built for home game rooms and small floors, not casino budgets.
note: Version 2.3 is in internal testing on our own bench machines. The current focus is G2S: making Gaming Manager connect to network-based machines exactly the way a real casino system does.

log.text: G2S work continues: machines are brought into play automatically after they connect, and meters are collected every minute.
Version 2.2 milestone finished. Work began on 2.3, a rebuild of the G2S connection modeled on how real casino systems talk to machines.
Bench session on a real IGT machine over SAS; fixes from that session went into 2.2.

details: Gaming Manager acts as the host system for your machines. It speaks SAS, the serial link found on nearly every machine since the late 1990s, and G2S, the newer network standard. It reads meters and events, prints and validates TITO tickets, moves credits to and from machines, and runs progressives and bonuses.

It comes in three editions. **Free** runs one machine with no account needed. **Advanced** is for home game rooms and collectors with several machines, with full SAS and G2S support. **Enterprise** is for small casinos and operators, with more machines, staff accounts and multi-location options. Pricing will be announced closer to release.

next.text: A control center for every machine (bonuses, credits, handpays, devices), staff accounts with roles, and a companion app for floor staff.
Player tracking with cards, sessions and points, plus optional cloud reporting.

name: GMOOCA Gaming Manager 3
summary: The next generation of Gaming Manager, adding the enterprise and regulatory functions that casinos, route operators and multi-site businesses need.
note: Actively in development alongside the 2.x releases. Version 2 lays the groundwork: the staff roles, audit trail and service host it adds are the foundation Version 3 builds on.
details: Version 2 is built for owners and small floors. Version 3 is built for businesses that answer to regulators: detailed audit trails, user accountability with dual control on sensitive actions, secure accounting and reporting, and management across multiple locations.

Gaming Manager 2 isn't intended for regulated, real-money floors. Version 3 is where that work happens, and we'll share more about its features and the path to regulated use as development moves forward.

name: GMOOCA SAS Gateway
summary: A small box that connects one machine's SAS port to your network with a single Ethernet cable, so you don't need to run a serial cable from every machine to your PC.
note: The first circuit board revision is designed and ready for fabrication. A smaller second revision is already planned.

log.text: Rev A board layout finished and reviewed; plan made for a smaller Rev B.
Design requirements locked: wired Ethernet, powered over the network cable, one machine per gateway.
Earlier EGM Module design reviewed; its lessons carried into the Gateway.

details: The Gateway sits next to the machine and handles SAS's strict timing right at the cabinet. It takes its power from the same network cable it talks over (Power over Ethernet), so there's no extra power supply to wire. GMOOCA will supply a cable for each manufacturer's SAS connector.

Its link to Gaming Manager is encrypted, each unit has its own identity, and its firmware updates over the network. On paid editions of Gaming Manager, each Gateway you pair adds a machine to your license.

name: Community forums
summary: Forums and a download library for owners, operators and collectors, all under one login. The same account will manage your Gaming Manager licenses.
note: Forum platform chosen and category structure drafted. Launch follows the platform purchase and setup.
details: The GMOOCA community will run on a dedicated forum platform at gmooca.org/Community, with discussion forums and a download library of GMOOCA-written guides and member-submitted original work.
Membership will be free at launch. See the [community page](/Community/) for the planned forum sections and ground rules.
